title: Tech Note: Handling Web Logins
author: David Adams
featured_technology: 4D Web Server (On Web Authentication, On Web Connection, 4DACTION)
HTTP Basic Authentication (401 Unauthorized, WWW-Authenticate header)

historical_commentary.text: This note explains a real usability flaw in 4D 2004's built-in On Web Authentication HTTP Basic Auth support — cancelling the browser's password dialog produced a blank, unhelpful screen — and provides a custom authentication pattern using On Web Connection and 4DACTION to show a friendly error/help page instead. The HTTP Basic Auth mechanics (401 status, WWW-Authenticate header, base64-encoded unencrypted credentials) are still accurate today, but the specific 4D Web Server architecture (On Web Authentication/On Web Connection hooks, 4DACTION calls) reflects 4D's pre-REST, pre-Qodly web stack, long since supplemented by modern session/token-based authentication approaches in current 4D web development.
related_updates: 4D's web server has since gained more modern session and authentication mechanisms beyond On Web Authentication/On Web Connection hooks
HTTP Basic Authentication itself remains standard and unchanged, but is now typically paired with HTTPS/SSL rather than used alone, as the note itself already cautions
